What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [redacted] 
Age: 28 years 
Sex: Female 

Date of Admission: [redacted] 
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Reason for Admission:
The patient presented with right hip pain after a fall and was diagnosed with a pathologic hip fracture. 

Clinical Course:
Following admission, the patient underwent radiographic and imaging studies which revealed lytic lesions in the femoral neck and intertrochanteric region as well as osseous destructive lesions in the lumbar spine. The bone scan was suggestive of metastatic disease. A biopsy revealed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with aggressive features and a germinal center subtype histology. The patient underwent a total right hip replacement and returned for follow-up evaluation.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was managed for the pathologic hip fracture and underwent biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of lymphoma. Following diagnosis, the patient underwent a total right hip replacement. The patient is scheduled for further evaluation and management by the oncology team. 

Discharge Medications: 
See the oncology team. 

Follow-up Plan: 
The patient is to follow up with the oncology team. 

Discharge Condition: 
The patient is stable.

text:
**Principal diagnosis: C83.3 Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma**

Rationale:
- The underlying condition that occasioned the admission and was treated is the lymphoma. The pathological fracture was due to lymphomatous bone involvement, and the biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. In ICD-10-AM, the fracture is coded as a manifestation of the neoplastic disease.
- The ICD-10-AM Alphabetic Index directs pathological fracture in neoplastic disease to M90.7* (Fracture in neoplastic disease). This is an asterisk code, so it cannot be the principal diagnosis. It is paired with the underlying etiology (dagger) code. The convention is to sequence the neoplasm code first.
- Bone involvement is a secondary site of the lymphoma, but lymphoma codes (C81–C88) are assigned by histologic type, not by site. The extranodal or bone involvement does not change the category. The 5th character for the site of nodes (e.g. C83.3 with extranodal/solid organ sites) may be applicable depending on your edition. Some editions of ICD-10-AM do not use a fifth character here.

Suggested additional codes:
- M90.7* Fracture in neoplastic disease (or M84.5* Pathological fracture in neoplastic disease, depending on edition), with a site code for the femoral neck.
- C79.5 Secondary malignant neoplasm of bone and bone marrow. This is typically not assigned for lymphoma, since the bone involvement is part of the lymphoma coding, so check local coding standards.
- ACHI procedure: total hip replacement (block 1489), plus the bone biopsy.

Please verify against your edition's Alphabetic Index and Tabular List and the local coding standards.
